newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Aznar says Spain to be part of EMU from outset.
newsitem.headline: Aznar says Spain to be part of EMU from outset.

text.p: Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar said Spain intended to be part of the future single European currency from the outset.

"The position of Spain is quite clear: to participate from the first moment in economic and monetary union (EMU)," Aznar told a news conference after arriving for a special summit of European Union leaders in Dublin.
Aznar said there had been a dramatic change of sentiment about Spain's prospects.
"Some months ago, there were doubts practically everywhere that Spain would be able to form part of the monetary union at the begining," he said.
"Now there are no doubts anywhere that Spain can and will be part of the monetary union at the beginning," he added.
Asked about reported differences between Spain and Italy over their strategy for joining EMU, he said:
"I want Italy to have the same success (as Spain) and be part of monetary union from the beginning."

Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi was reported to have suggested that the launch of the final stage of EMU should be delayed from 1 January, 1999 to allow countries such as Italy and Spain to be ready to join in. But Aznar rejected the suggestion in favour of meeting the original date.

Asked whether he had resolved his problems with Prodi, Aznar said: "The truth is there is nothing to sort out. I know there are some people who would like there to be problems but the truth is that there are no problems."
